requirements: Register every fully constructed waitable functor, including those with no current waiters. Track stable lifetimes and unregister before destruction; do not infer event identity from thread.event, which belongs to event-controlled assignment instructions.

Expose actual static threads_ heads and automatic per-context heads. Bind each reachable wait_next chain to live thread identities, reject cycles/duplicates/unknown objects, and compare the union to waiting_for_event flags at quiescent boundaries. Scheduled and event-wait lists have distinct owners despite sharing wait_next.

Observe initialized edge_ masks and all four bits_ histories, plus typed anyedge cache values and absent cache slots. Do not call get_*_value helpers during observation: they allocate missing caches. Use logical vector/string lengths and exact real bits, not object padding/capacity.

Cover automatic context allocation/reset/reuse/destruction explicitly when reachable; never reinterpret base template caches as per-context state. State addresses alone do not establish lifetime identity.

An event/or can share one functor across several input nets; preserve base_net_ and distinguish shared ownership from duplicate objects. Net connectivity and downstream fanout remain separate referents.

Observe event_ctls and last consistently. If controls are present, register and traverse their initialized typed payload, next, remaining count and destination referents; absence in this compiled fixture does not prove language-wide absence.

Mutate and restore real head pointers, edge histories/masks and initialized anyedge values before continuation. Require original/disabled/observed/restored complete output agreement and explicit wake/resuspend/empty-list coverage.
At each board boundary retain preceding thread/queue/filter/island/assignment/callback controls. Do not claim wait-event completion from pointer identity or successful serial output alone.
